title: The Hole Pays Out
setup: Steinitz against Sellman, Baltimore 1885, twenty-six moves later and not one sacrifice. Time to cash in the hole the lesson found.
hint: One square deep in Black's camp can never be attacked by a pawn again. Two knights could claim it — pick the one with nothing better to do.
explanation:
## The Idea

Twenty-six moves on, c6 is still a hole: Black's b- and d-pawns are past it for good.

{{Nac6}} lands there and hits the queen on b8 and the bishop on d8 at once. {{Qb7}} saves the queen, and {{Nxd8+}} takes the bishop with check.

The rook takes back and material is level, but Black's only dark-squared bishop is gone. Use the a5 knight: the one on d4 presses b5, e6 and f5, and moving it lets go of all three.
